intro: Nicosia learner drivers have more choice than ever in 2026, with instructors working both sides of the divided capital and across the busy suburbs.

schools.1868810b91eb4cc2: Merkan Driving School sits on Sht. Mehmet Kemal Sokak in north Nicosia and holds a perfect 5.0 rating from 44 reviews. The school is a strong pick for learners living in the northern districts of Lefkosa, with easy access to test routes around the old city walls. Instructors here are praised for patience with first-time drivers and for clear explanations of road signs in both Turkish and English. Lesson packages cover manual and automatic cars. The location makes it simple for students at nearby universities to fit lessons between classes. Merkan is a good fit if you want a small school where the same instructor follows your progress from the first lesson to the test.
schools.9073fa96208d89a8: Scholi Odigon P. Papaioannou is based on Nikou Theofanous 3 in Latsia, a busy suburb south of central Nicosia. The school has a 5.0 rating from 30 reviews, which is rare for a school of its size. Learners from Latsia, Geri and Strovolos can reach the office within minutes. The instructors are known for a calm teaching style and for using test routes that match the routes used by the Cyprus Department of Road Transport. Lessons cover the theory test, hazard awareness and the practical exam. The school works with both teenagers preparing for their first licence and adults returning to driving after years off the road.
schools.3b5323725a65945b: Deniz Yagizerler Sofor Okulu is a small driving school in north Nicosia with a 5.0 rating from 8 reviews. The school is a steady choice for learners who want one-to-one attention and a flexible timetable. Instructors focus on the north Nicosia test format, including parallel parking, hill starts and city centre driving. Students often mention the friendly atmosphere and the clear pricing. The school covers both manual and automatic cars and accepts learners from age 16 for moped lessons and 18 for full car lessons. If you live near the Dereboyu area or work in the city centre, the location is handy for evening lessons after work.
schools.c99f25bf7289098b: Tilki Sofor Okulu, at plus code 59R7+8Q7 in north Nicosia, holds a 5.0 rating. The school is small but well regarded by the learners who have trained there. Lessons are offered in Turkish and English, which helps international students from the nearby universities. The school covers the standard north Nicosia practical test, with practice on roundabouts, traffic lights and reverse parking. Instructors take time to explain the local road code, which differs in some details from the south. If you prefer a quiet school where you are not just a number on a booking sheet, Tilki is worth a look.
schools.2aa490ecf1175ea5: This branch of Tilki Sofor Okulu is on Istanbul Sokak in north Nicosia and shares the strong reputation of the main office, with a 5.0 rating. The Istanbul Sokak location gives easy access to test routes through residential streets and main avenues. Instructors run short, focused lessons that suit students with packed schedules. Lessons cover both car and motorbike training, and the school helps with theory test preparation. Learners say the instructors are punctual and clear with feedback after each session. For drivers living or studying near the Yenisehir district, this is one of the closer options for full driver training.
schools.bfd5d8d04364fd4c: Nicosia Driving School on Archiepiskopou Makariou III 75d is the largest school in the capital, with 1182 reviews and a 4.9 rating. The office sits on the main avenue running through the centre, which makes it reachable from almost every neighbourhood in the south. The school runs a full timetable from early morning to evening, and lessons can be booked online. Instructors cover manual, automatic and motorbike training. The school is well known for high pass rates on the Cyprus practical test and for clear theory classes in Greek and English. With so many instructors on staff, it is usually easy to find a time slot that fits your week.
schools.a70188f63b82b3ba: Stylianos Stylianou Driving School is based on P. Liasidi in Lakatamia and has a 4.9 rating from 251 reviews. The school is a popular choice for learners in Lakatamia, Anthoupoli and the western suburbs of Nicosia. Stylianos and his team teach in Greek and English and focus on building confidence step by step. Lessons include city driving, motorway practice on the A1 and parking drills on quiet side streets. The school helps students book the theory test and the practical test, and gives mock tests before the real exam. Reviewers often mention the relaxed teaching style and the willingness to give extra time when needed.
schools.7ff98b419abcc3ad: G.T Mygdalia Driving School on Ilia Papakyriakou 5B in Engomi has a 4.9 rating from 51 reviews. Engomi is home to the University of Cyprus, so the school is popular with students living on campus or in nearby flats. The school covers car and motorbike lessons and helps learners through both the theory and practical tests. Instructors run lessons in Greek and English. The location gives quick access to test routes through Engomi, Aglantzia and the centre. Reviewers praise the clear lesson plans and the patient instructors who take time to explain mistakes rather than just point them out.
schools.3c85a6e624cf5d5d: Vizyon Surucu Kursu is on Sht. Halil Mustafa Sokak in the Kizilay area of north Nicosia, with a 4.9 rating from 45 reviews. The school offers car and motorbike lessons in Turkish and English. Instructors focus on real-world skills, including night driving, wet road handling and busy junction work. The school is a strong choice for learners who want a structured course with set milestones. Lessons can be booked as single sessions or as full packages. Reviewers mention fair pricing and instructors who keep calm even with nervous first-time drivers. The Kizilay location is handy for learners living in the inner districts of north Nicosia.
schools.969ab4fd75ea3ccc: Katsaris Driving School on Andrea Zakou in Latsia rounds out the top ten with a 4.9 rating from 35 reviews. The school is a solid local option for learners in Latsia, Geri and the southeastern suburbs. Instructors cover the full Cyprus driving syllabus, from basic car control to motorway driving on the route towards Larnaca. Lessons are offered in Greek and English. The school helps with theory test booking and runs practice tests before the practical exam. Reviewers say the instructors are honest about when a student is ready for the test, which saves money on extra attempts. The office is easy to reach from the Latsia industrial area.

closing: Driving in Nicosia is a different experience from driving anywhere else in Cyprus, and that shapes how local schools teach. The capital is split between the Republic of Cyprus in the south and the northern part under Turkish Cypriot administration, with the Green Line running through the centre. Learners need to pick a school on the side where they plan to take the test, since the two systems use separate licences and separate test routes. In the south, the main test centre handles candidates from across the district, and instructors focus on routes through Strovolos, Aglantzia, Lakatamia and Latsia. In the north, test routes cover the streets around Dereboyu, Kizilay and the old city. Traffic in Nicosia builds up sharply in the morning rush between 7:30 and 9:00 and again from 13:00 to 14:30 when schools finish. Archiepiskopou Makariou III Avenue, Griva Digeni and the road into Engomi can slow to a crawl. Good instructors use these busy periods to teach lane discipline, gap judgement and patience at traffic lights. The A1 motorway towards Limassol gives learners a safe stretch for higher-speed practice, and most schools include at least one motorway lesson before the test. Roundabouts are common across the capital, and the test almost always includes several. Parking practice usually takes place in quieter streets in Latsia, Engomi or Lakatamia, where there is room to set up cones without holding up other drivers. Summer heat is a real factor: cars without working air conditioning are hard work in July and August, so check the lesson car before you book. Winter brings short bursts of heavy rain that flood low-lying junctions, and instructors use these days to teach wet weather skills. The theory test is taken on a computer and covers road signs, right of way and safe distances. Most schools run short theory classes in Greek, Turkish or English. Book lessons early in the week if you want weekend slots, since these fill fast. Ask any school for a sample lesson before signing a full package, and check that the instructor is licensed by the Department of Road Transport in the south or the equivalent authority in the north.

faq.q: How old do I need to be to start driving lessons in Nicosia?
faq.a: You can apply for a learner permit at 17 and a half in the south, and start lessons straight after. The full car licence is issued at 18. Moped lessons can start earlier.

faq.q: How much do driving lessons cost in Nicosia in 2026?
faq.a: A single lesson usually costs between 25 and 40 euros. Full packages with theory support and test booking range from 350 to 600 euros, depending on the school and the number of hours.

faq.q: Can I take lessons in English in Nicosia?
faq.a: Yes. Most schools in both the north and south of the city offer lessons in English. Some also teach in Russian, Arabic or Romanian. Ask the school before booking.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a driving licence in Nicosia?
faq.a: Most learners need two to three months from the first lesson to passing the practical test. This depends on how often you take lessons and how quickly test slots open up.

faq.q: Is the test the same in north and south Nicosia?
faq.a: No. The two sides use separate licensing systems with different theory tests, practical routes and licence formats. Pick a school on the side where you want to take the test and live.
